subproblem.title: Upper bound on compact sets from sub-subsequence comparisons on thickenings (parent step 2(b); Simon 7.2.4 (12)–(13))
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and let μ and μ_j (j ∈ ℕ) be Borel measures on ℝ^P (Measure (Euclid P)). Assume (a) μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P; and (b′) for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P, every ε > 0 and every strictly increasing ψ : ℕ → ℕ there are a set W ⊆ ℝ^P with K ⊆ W ⊆ thickening(ε, K) = {x : infEdist(x, K) < ε} and a strictly increasing φ′ : ℕ → ℕ with limsup_{i→∞} μ_{ψ(φ′(i))}(W) ≤ μ(W). Then limsup_{j→∞} μ_j(K) ≤ μ(K) for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P (lim sup in [0, ∞]).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μs : ℕ → Measure (Euclid P)) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)), (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → μ K < ∞) → (∀ (K : Set (Euclid P)) (ε : ℝ), IsCompact K → 0 < ε → ∀ ψ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono ψ → ∃ W : Set (Euclid P), K ⊆ W ∧ W ⊆ thickening ε K ∧ ∃ φ' : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ' ∧ limsup (fun i => μs (ψ (φ' i)) W) atTop ≤ μ W) → ∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → limsup (fun j => μs j K) atTop ≤ μ K
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2(b) of the parent proof (Simon 7.2.4: (12), chapter-07.txt line 260; the bound before (13), lines 265–275; (13), line 276; and the subsequence-of-subsequence remark, lines 278–280). The current-specific input (the local comparison with the competitor S := C, converted to measures) is abstracted into hypothesis (b′); the remaining measure-theoretic argument is copied from the parent. No sibling result is used.
1. Fix a compact K and put L := limsup_j μ_j(K) ∈ [0, ∞].
2. (Claim: L ≤ μ(thickening(ε, K)) for every ε > 0.) Fix ε > 0 and suppose instead that a := μ(thickening(ε, K)) < L. Since [0, ∞] is densely ordered, choose b with a < b < L. Since b < limsup_j μ_j(K), μ_j(K) > b for infinitely many j (frequently in atTop; Mathlib frequently_lt_of_lt_limsup). Hence there is a strictly increasing ψ : ℕ → ℕ with μ_{ψ(i)}(K) > b for all i (Mathlib Filter.extraction_of_frequently_atTop).
3. Apply (b′) to K, ε and ψ: there are W with K ⊆ W ⊆ thickening(ε, K) and a strictly increasing φ′ with limsup_i μ_{ψ(φ′(i))}(W) ≤ μ(W). By monotonicity of measures, μ_{ψ(φ′(i))}(W) ≥ μ_{ψ(φ′(i))}(K) > b for every i, so limsup_i μ_{ψ(φ′(i))}(W) ≥ b (Mathlib le_limsup_of_frequently_le). Also μ(W) ≤ μ(thickening(ε, K)) = a. Hence b ≤ limsup_i μ_{ψ(φ′(i))}(W) ≤ μ(W) ≤ a < b, a contradiction. This proves the claim.
4. (Continuity from above.) K is compact, hence closed. thickening(1, K) ⊆ cthickening(1, K), and cthickening(1, K) is compact (closed and bounded in ℝ^P; Mathlib IsCompact.cthickening), so μ(thickening(1, K)) ≤ μ(cthickening(1, K)) < ∞ by (a). The open sets thickening(r, K) decrease as r ↓ 0 and their intersection is closure K = K. By continuity of measure from above (Mathlib tendsto_measure_thickening_of_isClosed, which needs exactly one finite μ(thickening(R, K)) with R > 0 and K closed), μ(thickening(r, K)) → μ(K) as r → 0⁺.
5. By step 2, L ≤ μ(thickening(r, K)) for every r > 0. Since the right side tends to μ(K) as r → 0⁺ and the order interval [L, ∞] is closed, L ≤ μ(K). As K was arbitrary, the claim holds for every compact K. ∎
proof_key_steps: If μ(thickening(ε, K)) < b < limsup_j μ_j(K), extract a strictly increasing ψ with μ_{ψ(i)}(K) > b for all i.
Hypothesis (b′) along ψ gives W ⊇ K inside thickening(ε, K) and φ′ with limsup_i μ_{ψ(φ′(i))}(W) ≤ μ(W); monotonicity gives b ≤ limsup ≤ μ(W) ≤ μ(thickening(ε, K)) < b, a contradiction.
μ(thickening(1, K)) < ∞ by finiteness on the compact cthickening(1, K); continuity from above gives μ(thickening(r, K)) → μ(K) as r ↓ 0, hence limsup_j μ_j(K) ≤ μ(K).

audit.reason: The bad-subsequence extraction and sub-subsequence comparison establish every thickening bound. Compactness supplies a finite thickening, permitting continuity from above. Only measure monotonicity is used on W, so no measurability assumption is missing.

subproblem.title: Lower semicontinuity of mass under weak convergence on exhausting domains, along any subsequence (parent's L3; Simon 6.2.14)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ. For j ∈ ℕ let U_j ⊆ ℝ^P be any set and S_j ∈ 𝒟_n(U_j) (GeometricCurrentOn (U_j) n), and let C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P). Assume (1) for every R ∈ ℝ, closedBall(0, R) ⊆ U_j for all sufficiently large j; and (2) S_j ⇀ C in ℝ^P in the sense of ConvergesWeakly: currentEval(S_j, ω) → C(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P). Then for every strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ and every set O ⊆ ℝ^P, M_O(C) ≤ liminf_{i→∞} M_O(S_{φ(i)}) in [0, ∞]. Here M_O(T) = T.massOn O = sup{max(T(ω), 0) : ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(dom T), tsupport ω ⊆ O, |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x} ∈ [0, ∞] (SimonGMT massOn, Simon 6.2.5, Euclidean coefficient norm), spt is GeometricCurrentOn.support (Simon 6.2.11), and currentEval(S_j, ω) = S_j(ω) if ω is a test form with tsupport ω ⊆ U_j and 0 otherwise.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Us : ℕ → Set (Euclid P)) (Ss : (j : ℕ) → GeometricCurrentOn (Us j) n) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), (∀ R : ℝ, ∀ᶠ j in atTop, closedBall (0 : Euclid P) R ⊆ Us j) → ConvergesWeakly Ss C → ∀ φ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ → ∀ O : Set (Euclid P), C.massOn O ≤ liminf (fun i => (Ss (φ i)).massOn O) atTop
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: preliminary L3 of the parent proof (lower semicontinuity of mass, Simon Ch. 6, 2.14, chapter-06.txt line 313 ('mass is trivially lower semi-continuous with respect to weak convergence'), used in Simon 7.2.4 at chapter-07.txt lines 262–263 and in (14), line 283), along the weak convergence on exhausting domains of the parent statement. It is generalized from bounded open O to arbitrary O, and openness of the U_j is not used: the parent used boundedness of O only to place tsupport ω in a ball, and that already follows from the compactness of tsupport ω. SimonGMT's WeaklyConvergesOn.massOn_le_liminf covers only a fixed common domain, so it does not apply directly. No sibling result is used.
Notation. For T ∈ 𝒟_n(V) and O ⊆ ℝ^P let A_V(O) := massAdmissibleOn V n O = {ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V) : tsupport ω ⊆ O and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x}. Then M_O(T) = sup{ofReal(T(ω)) : ω ∈ A_V(O)} ∈ [0, ∞], where ofReal(t) = max(t, 0).
1. Fix a strictly increasing φ and a set O. Since M_O(C) is the supremum of ofReal(C(ω)) over ω ∈ A_{ℝ^P}(O), it suffices to show ofReal(C(ω)) ≤ liminf_i M_O(S_{φ(i)}) for each ω ∈ A_{ℝ^P}(O).
2. Fix ω ∈ A_{ℝ^P}(O). Being a test form, ω has compact support, so tsupport ω is compact, hence bounded, and tsupport ω ⊆ closedBall(0, R) for some R ∈ ℝ.
3. By (1) there is j₀ with closedBall(0, R) ⊆ U_j for all j ≥ j₀. Since φ is strictly increasing, φ(i) ≥ i, so for every i ≥ j₀ we get closedBall(0, R) ⊆ U_{φ(i)} and hence tsupport ω ⊆ U_{φ(i)}.
4. For such i, the underlying form of ω is a test form with tsupport in U_{φ(i)}. So it defines an element ω_i ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U_{φ(i)}), and by the definition of currentEval, currentEval(S_{φ(i)}, ω) = S_{φ(i)}(ω_i). The two conditions defining A_{U_{φ(i)}}(O) (tsupport ⊆ O and pointwise norm ≤ 1) concern only the underlying form, so ω_i ∈ A_{U_{φ(i)}}(O). Hence ofReal(currentEval(S_{φ(i)}, ω)) = ofReal(S_{φ(i)}(ω_i)) ≤ M_O(S_{φ(i)}) for every i ≥ j₀.
5. By (2), applied to ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P), currentEval(S_j, ω) → C(ω) as j → ∞. Since φ(i) → ∞, also currentEval(S_{φ(i)}, ω) → C(ω) as i → ∞. ofReal : ℝ → [0, ∞] is continuous, so ofReal(currentEval(S_{φ(i)}, ω)) → ofReal(C(ω)).
6. Therefore ofReal(C(ω)) = liminf_i ofReal(currentEval(S_{φ(i)}, ω)) ≤ liminf_i M_O(S_{φ(i)}). The equality holds because the sequence converges. The inequality holds because liminf is monotone under an eventual termwise inequality (step 4); in the complete lattice [0, ∞] no boundedness side conditions arise.
7. Taking the supremum over ω ∈ A_{ℝ^P}(O) (step 1) gives M_O(C) ≤ liminf_i M_O(S_{φ(i)}). ∎
proof_key_steps: Reduce to one admissible ω for C on O, since M_O(C) is a supremum.
tsupport ω is compact, so it lies in some closedBall(0, R) ⊆ U_{φ(i)} for all large i; there ω is admissible for S_{φ(i)} and ofReal(currentEval(S_{φ(i)}, ω)) ≤ M_O(S_{φ(i)}).
currentEval(S_{φ(i)}, ω) → C(ω), so ofReal(C(ω)) is the liminf of these values and is ≤ liminf_i M_O(S_{φ(i)}); take the supremum over ω.

audit.reason: Each test form has compact support eventually contained in the exhausting domains, including along the subsequence. Weak convergence, continuity of ofReal and eventual liminf monotonicity prove the bound. The generalization to arbitrary O and U_j is justified.

subproblem.title: Radon-criterion bounds for the mass measures: finiteness on compacts, compact lim sup, open lim inf (parent step 2(a)–(c); Simon 7.2.4 (12)–(14))
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ. For j ∈ ℕ let U_j ⊆ ℝ^P be open and S_j ∈ 𝒟_n(U_j), and let C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P). Assume (1) for every R ∈ ℝ, closedBall(0, R) ⊆ U_j for all large j; (2) S_j ⇀ C in ℝ^P (ConvergesWeakly); (3) (local comparison) for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P, every ε > 0 and every strictly increasing ψ : ℕ → ℕ there are an open W with K ⊆ W ⊆ thickening(ε, K) = {x : infEdist(x, K) < ε} and a strictly increasing φ′ : ℕ → ℕ such that limsup_{i→∞} M_W(S_{ψ(φ′(i))}) ≤ M_W(S) for every integer multiplicity S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with SameBoundary S C (∂S = ∂C, vacuous for n = 0) and spt(S − C) ⊆ K. Let R_j ∈ IMRep(U_j, n) represent S_j for every j, and let R ∈ IMRep(ℝ^P, n) represent C. Write μ_j := R_j.measure = θ_j Hⁿ⌞M_j and μ := R.measure. Then (a) μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P; (b) limsup_j μ_j(K) ≤ μ(K) for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P; and (c) μ(G) ≤ liminf_j μ_j(G) for every bounded open G ⊆ ℝ^P (lim sup and lim inf in [0, ∞]). These are exactly the hypotheses of radon_criterion for (μ_j) and μ. Here M_O(T) = T.massOn O = sup{max(T(ω), 0) : ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(dom T), tsupport ω ⊆ O, |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x} ∈ [0, ∞] (SimonGMT massOn, Simon 6.2.5, Euclidean coefficient norm), spt is GeometricCurrentOn.support (Simon 6.2.11), and currentEval(S_j, ω) = S_j(ω) if ω is a test form with tsupport ω ⊆ U_j and 0 otherwise.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2(a)–(c) of the parent proof (Simon 7.2.4 (12)–(14), chapter-07.txt lines 260–288, including the subsequence-of-subsequence remark of lines 278–280). Siblings used: mass_eq_measure (L2), mass_lsc (L3), limsup_criterion (LIM) and imrep_local_finiteness. The final application of radon_criterion stays in the selected parent node, where that result is a resolved dependency. Notation: M_G(T) = T.massOn G.
0. By mass_eq_measure: (i) M_G(C) = μ(G) for every open G, since ℝ^P is open and R represents C; (ii) M_G(S_j) = μ_j(G) for every open G and every j, since U_j is open and R_j represents S_j.
1. (a) Let K be compact. K ⊆ ℝ^P, so imrep_local_finiteness (with U := ℝ^P and R) gives μ(K) ≠ ∞, i.e. μ(K) < ∞. (This is the parent's computation μ(K) = ∫_{M_R ∩ K} θ_R dHⁿ < ∞ by locallyIntegrable_mult.)
2. (c) Let G be open; boundedness is not needed. By (i), mass_lsc with φ := id and O := G, and (ii) applied termwise: μ(G) = M_G(C) ≤ liminf_j M_G(S_j) = liminf_j μ_j(G).
3. (C is an admissible competitor for itself.) (α) C is integer multiplicity, witnessed by R. (β) SameBoundary C C: SameBoundary is defined by cases on the degree; for n = 0 it is True, and for n = m + 1 it is C.boundary = C.boundary, which holds by reflexivity. (γ) spt(C − C) = ∅. For every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P), (C − C)(ω) = C(ω) − C(ω) = 0. Given x ∈ ℝ^P, the ball B := ball(x, 1) is open; its closure lies in the compact set closedBall(x, 1), so it is compact; closure B ⊆ ℝ^P; and C − C vanishes on every form supported in B. Thus B belongs to the family whose union is the zero region of C − C, and x ∈ B. So the zero region is ℝ^P and spt(C − C) = ℝ^P ∖ ℝ^P = ∅. In particular spt(C − C) ⊆ K for every K.
4. (b) We verify the hypotheses of LIM for the measures μ_j and μ. Its hypothesis (a) is step 1. For its hypothesis (b′), let K be compact, ε > 0 and ψ strictly increasing. Hypothesis (3) gives an open W with K ⊆ W ⊆ thickening(ε, K) and a strictly increasing φ′ such that limsup_i M_W(S_{ψ(φ′(i))}) ≤ M_W(S) for every admissible S. Taking S := C, admissible by step 3, gives limsup_i M_W(S_{ψ(φ′(i))}) ≤ M_W(C). W is open, so (ii) gives M_W(S_{ψ(φ′(i))}) = μ_{ψ(φ′(i))}(W) for each i, and (i) gives M_W(C) = μ(W). So limsup_i μ_{ψ(φ′(i))}(W) ≤ μ(W), which is (b′) for this W and φ′. LIM now yields limsup_j μ_j(K) ≤ μ(K) for every compact K.
5. Steps 1, 4 and 2 give the three conclusions (a), (b) and (c). ∎
proof_key_steps: mass_eq_measure converts masses on open sets to weights: M_G(C) = μ(G) and M_G(S_j) = μ_j(G).
(a) from imrep_local_finiteness; (c) from mass_lsc with φ = id.
C is an admissible competitor for itself: integer multiplicity via R, SameBoundary C C by cases on n, and spt(C − C) = ∅ since C − C vanishes on every ball.
(b) The local comparison with S := C, converted to weights, is hypothesis (b′) of limsup_criterion, which gives limsup_j μ_j(K) ≤ μ(K).

audit.reason: The proof establishes all three exact RADON hypotheses. R witnesses integer multiplicity of C; boundary reflexivity and the ball-based zero-support argument make C an admissible competitor. The declared dependencies then yield both limit bounds.

subproblem.title: The weak limit C is minimizing in ℝ^P (parent step 1; Simon 7.2.4 (8) and its localization)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ. For j ∈ ℕ let U_j ⊆ ℝ^P be any set and S_j ∈ 𝒟_n(U_j), and let C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) be integer multiplicity (IsIntegerMultiplicity C). Assume (1) for every R ∈ ℝ, closedBall(0, R) ⊆ U_j for all large j; (2) S_j ⇀ C in ℝ^P (ConvergesWeakly: currentEval(S_j, ω) → C(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P)); (3) (local comparison) for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P, every ε > 0 and every strictly increasing ψ : ℕ → ℕ there are an open W with K ⊆ W ⊆ thickening(ε, K) = {x : infEdist(x, K) < ε} and a strictly increasing φ′ : ℕ → ℕ such that limsup_{i→∞} M_W(S_{ψ(φ′(i))}) ≤ M_W(S) for every integer multiplicity S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with SameBoundary S C (∂S = ∂C, vacuous for n = 0) and spt(S − C) ⊆ K. Then C is minimizing in ℝ^P (IsMinimizingIn C univ). That is, C is integer multiplicity, and M_W(C) ≤ M_W(S) whenever W ⊆ ℝ^P is open with compact closure, S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) is integer multiplicity, SameBoundary S C holds, and spt(S − C) is compact and contained in W. Here M_O(T) = T.massOn O = sup{max(T(ω), 0) : ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(dom T), tsupport ω ⊆ O, |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x} ∈ [0, ∞] (SimonGMT massOn, Simon 6.2.5, Euclidean coefficient norm), spt is GeometricCurrentOn.support (Simon 6.2.11), and currentEval(S_j, ω) = S_j(ω) if ω is a test form with tsupport ω ⊆ U_j and 0 otherwise.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent proof (Simon 7.2.4, (8) and its localization: chapter-07.txt lines 226–229, with the comparison (12), line 260, and the lower semicontinuity of lines 262–263). Siblings used: mass_lsc (the parent's L3), mass_eq_measure (the parent's L2), mass_agree_off_support (the parent's use of V: S and C agree on forms supported in O = ℝ^P ∖ spt(S − C)), and measure_agree_on_borel with imrep_local_finiteness, which together with the previous two give the case U₁ = U₂ = ℝ^P, W := O of MEAS that the parent applies ('μ_S = μ_C on Borel subsets of O, in particular on W ∖ W′'). The argument is the parent's, step for step; only the appeal to MEAS is unfolded into these accepted components (MEAS is not available to a child of this node). Notation: M_G(T) = T.massOn G; all quantities lie in [0, ∞].
1. IsMinimizingIn C ℝ^P has two parts. The first, IsIntegerMultiplicity C, is a hypothesis. For the second, fix an open W with CompactlyContained W ℝ^P and an integer multiplicity S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with SameBoundary S C such that K := spt(S − C) is compact and K ⊆ ℝ^P ∩ W = W. We must show M_W(C) ≤ M_W(S).
2. K is compact, W is open and K ⊆ W, so there is ε > 0 with thickening(ε, K) ⊆ W (Mathlib IsCompact.exists_thickening_subset_open).
3. Apply hypothesis (3) with K, ε and ψ := id, which is strictly increasing. This gives an open W′ with K ⊆ W′ ⊆ thickening(ε, K) ⊆ W and a strictly increasing φ′ such that limsup_i M_{W′}(S_{φ′(i)}) ≤ M_{W′}(S′) for every integer multiplicity S′ ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with SameBoundary S′ C and spt(S′ − C) ⊆ K. S itself qualifies, since spt(S − C) = K ⊆ K. Hence limsup_i M_{W′}(S_{φ′(i)}) ≤ M_{W′}(S).
4. By mass_lsc with φ := φ′ and O := W′: M_{W′}(C) ≤ liminf_i M_{W′}(S_{φ′(i)}) ≤ limsup_i M_{W′}(S_{φ′(i)}) ≤ M_{W′}(S). Here liminf ≤ limsup holds along atTop in the complete lattice [0, ∞].
5. Let R_C and R_S be integer multiplicity representations of C and S (they exist by IsIntegerMultiplicity C and IsIntegerMultiplicity S), and put μ_C := R_C.measure and μ_S := R_S.measure. By mass_eq_measure (U := ℝ^P, which is open), M_G(C) = μ_C(G) and M_G(S) = μ_S(G) for every open G ⊆ ℝ^P.
6. O := ℝ^P ∖ K is open, since K is compact and hence closed. Let G ⊆ O be open. Then G ∩ K = ∅ and spt(S − C) ⊆ K, so mass_agree_off_support (with U := ℝ^P, S := S, T := C, K := K, G := G) gives M_G(S) = M_G(C). By step 5, μ_S(G) = μ_C(G).
7. By imrep_local_finiteness (with U := ℝ^P and R := R_S), μ_S(K′) ≠ ∞ for every compact K′ ⊆ ℝ^P, in particular for every compact K′ ⊆ O. By measure_agree_on_borel (with O, μ := μ_S and ν := μ_C), using step 6 and this finiteness, μ_S(A) = μ_C(A) for every Borel set A ⊆ O.
8. W ∖ W′ is a Borel set (a difference of open sets) and W ∖ W′ ⊆ O because K ⊆ W′. By step 7, μ_S(W ∖ W′) = μ_C(W ∖ W′).
9. W′ ⊆ thickening(ε, K) ⊆ W and W′ is Borel, so μ(W) = μ(W′) + μ(W ∖ W′) for every measure μ on ℝ^P (Mathlib measure_inter_add_sdiff with W ∩ W′ = W′). Using steps 4, 5 and 8: M_W(C) = μ_C(W) = μ_C(W′) + μ_C(W ∖ W′) = M_{W′}(C) + μ_S(W ∖ W′) ≤ M_{W′}(S) + μ_S(W ∖ W′) = μ_S(W′) + μ_S(W ∖ W′) = μ_S(W) = M_W(S). These manipulations are valid in [0, ∞] without any finiteness assumption (addition is monotone in [0, ∞]).
10. Since W and S were arbitrary, C is minimizing in ℝ^P (IsMinimizingIn C univ). ∎
proof_key_steps: For a competitor S with K := spt(S − C) compact and ⊆ W, choose ε with thickening(ε, K) ⊆ W and apply the local comparison with ψ = id: an open W′ with K ⊆ W′ ⊆ W and φ′ with limsup_i M_{W′}(S_{φ′(i)}) ≤ M_{W′}(S).
mass_lsc along φ′ and liminf ≤ limsup give M_{W′}(C) ≤ M_{W′}(S).

mass_eq_measure turns masses on open sets into weights; mass_agree_off_support gives μ_S = μ_C on open subsets of O = ℝ^P ∖ K, and measure_agree_on_borel with imrep_local_finiteness extends this to Borel subsets of O, in particular W ∖ W′.
Additivity: μ_C(W) = μ_C(W′) + μ_C(W ∖ W′) ≤ μ_S(W′) + μ_S(W ∖ W′) = μ_S(W), i.e. M_W(C) ≤ M_W(S).

audit.reason: Local comparison and lower semicontinuity give the inequality near the difference support. The declared locality components identify the measures on the remaining Borel region; additivity extends the inequality to W without subtracting infinite quantities.
